fixed.explanation: In the internal:role branch, name and description both set options.exact from attr.caseSensitive and throw on a mismatch. A regex value has no meaningful exactness, so mixing a regex with an exact string makes the check throw. The caller then falls back to the raw selector. The fix applies the exactness check and assignment only to string values.

query.intent: Code that converts an internal selector string (internal:role=...) into a readable locator expression (getByRole with name and description options) fails to handle regex vs string values for name and description, falling back to the raw selector. Likely the selector-to-locator generator/parser for role engine attributes.
query.symptom: Role locators with a regex name and string description (or reverse) are printed as raw internal selectors instead of getByRole(...) locator text.

history.analysis: The selector-to-locator conversion happens in locatorGenerators.ts (innerAsLocators), which handles internal:role. getByRoleSelector shows name and description are escaped as strings or regexes, so the role handling probably mishandles mixed regex/string types and throws, which falls back to the raw selector. I need to see that role branch.
